prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of the incretin hormone GLP-1 and its active forms, which enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B046 alone, with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Having read the full first round, I note that every member reached the same configuration with the same reservations, which makes it more important to test the case than to count it. The case holds on content. The arc runs from proglucagon processing and the identification of GLP-1(7-36) as the active form, through glucose-dependent insulin secretion and the central and gastric effects on appetite, to therapies with cardiovascular and renal outcome benefit in large independent trials. It is old enough to be thoroughly replicated, and the question of maturity does not arise. Holst, Drucker and Mojsov cover secretion physiology, mechanism with translational proof of concept, and the active peptide, which is the discovery side of the story. On the chair's question about the citation, I now prefer to name the physiology of GLP-1 and its active forms first and to name the therapies only as the consequence, as Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius word it. That claims the discovery without ruling on which group was first to each step. I would keep a single prize part. A second part would force one of the three GLP-1 names out under the cap, and none of the second candidates is strong enough to justify that.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakness, and round 1 did not remove it. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide relative to Habener's group is contested, and the supplied material does not let me settle it. Knudsen is excluded, so the prize can be read as honouring physiology over the long-acting analogues that reached patients. A committee that stops at physiology must accept that criticism, and one that includes drug development must accept that it is crediting optimisation. A related risk is that I am keeping Mojsov partly because the chain needs a first link, and that argument could be turned against any name. I hold the configuration because the alternatives do not look better. I do not claim it is free of contest.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius would consider Knudsen in place of Mojsov if the committee treats drug development as essential, and she is unsure whether Mojsov's priority is sound enough to keep her.
responses.response: I take the Knudsen swap seriously, but I would not make it. Knudsen's long-acting analogue design is real and decisive for the products, yet it builds on an active peptide and a receptor pharmacology that already existed. Replacing Mojsov with Knudsen changes the prize from a discovery prize into a development prize, and the committee has applied that line inconsistently in the past, which is no reason to cross it now. The Habener question does not settle the matter either. Even if Mojsov's priority is shared, the identification and synthesis of the active peptide is a necessary link, and the usual remedy is a shared credit within the three-person limit, not removal. If the committee judges her claim too weak to defend, I would drop her and not substitute Knudsen, which leaves Holst and Drucker as a thinner but cleaner fallback. I think that is a worse outcome than the trio.

responses.point: Perlmann chooses the physiology reading over the inclusion of drug development, accepting that a prize which folds in development would be crediting an industrial optimisation step, and he also flags the Eshhar gap in B040.
responses.response: I agree with his reasoning that the prize should stay with the discovery and not extend to its industrial optimisation, and I think it is a stronger argument than the one from precedent. The weak point in it is that the line between discovery and optimisation is not sharp for GLP-1, because Drucker's translational work and the move from the native peptide to a durable agonist are connected. The reasoning therefore only works if the citation says what is being honoured and does not imply that the physiology alone made the medicine. On Eshhar I have moved a little since round 1. The gap is a real defect of B040 and I would not treat it as a footnote. This is another reason to keep B040 as an alternative and not to attach it to B046 as a second part.

responses.point: El-Manira holds optogenetics as the most original method on the list, with precedent for honouring enabling methods, and asks which second achievement could share the prize without displacing a GLP-1 laureate.
responses.response: His question has an answer only if the three-person cap is respected, and under the cap I do not think any second part can be added without weakening B046. I accept his point that methods have been honoured and that optogenetics changed circuit neuroscience, and as a user of enabling methods I may be too ready to find such a case attractive. That is a reason to be careful with my own judgment. The six-name allocation still has no principled three-person cut among Bamberg, Boyden, Deisseroth, Hegemann, Miesenboeck and Nagel. The discovery of the channelrhodopsins and their neuronal deployment are tightly linked, and any cut would be arbitrary. That settles B049 as an alternative for a later year, not a partner this year.

responses.point: Sandberg limits B040 to June and Sadelain and says that if the committee treats drug development as the discovery, B046 is incomplete; he also lists B031 as an alternative.
responses.response: I agree with the June and Sadelain pair, and I note that this is the same logic as my position on B046. In both cases I credit the people who made the decisive design and the demonstration of its effect, and I leave the forerunners to the committee's deliberations. I disagree that B046 is incomplete without development, for the reason I gave to Wahren-Herlenius. On B031 I accept that it has the cleanest attribution on the list and I still rank it below B040 because the translation is early. His point on PERK, ATF6 and the integrated stress response is a fair limit on what Mori and Walter can be credited with, and I would want that stated in any citation. It does not change my ordering for this year.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority relative to Habener's group is settled enough to keep her in the trio. I cannot resolve this from the supplied record.
Whether a citation that names only the physiology can avoid being read as a statement about who discovered what in the early GLP-1 literature.
Whether the discovery and optimisation line I am drawing against Knudsen is as sharp as I have argued, given Drucker's translational work.
Whether B040 with June and Sadelain would be a better single prize in a later year once the Eshhar gap and long-term safety are clearer.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. No specific conflict is apparent for B046, B040 or B049. My spatial-transcriptomics and single-cell work, and eight recorded co-authored works with Rickard Sandberg (count not audited), are not tied to any shortlisted candidate. B024 was not proposed by anyone in round 1 and I am not advancing it. If it came up again I would flag my methodological proximity and ask whether recusal is needed.
